items.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back a shared robots.txt AI-training opt-out signal
items.summary: The four companies said on October 30 that they will honor a common signal websites can add to robots.txt to express AI-training preferences that apply across providers, an effort that grew out of an IETF AI Preferences working-group draft. It gives publishers one place to set training preferences instead of negotiating with each AI company separately, though compliance is voluntary and implementation details are still being worked out.

items.headline: Microsoft's AI Safety & Privacy Standard for US schools takes effect
items.summary: A set of enforceable AI data-protection terms Microsoft negotiated with the American Federation of Teachers and the United Federation of Teachers became effective for US school districts on November 1, barring Microsoft from training models on student data and requiring human oversight of AI decisions affecting students. It gives districts contractual remedies, including termination rights, if the terms are violated.

items.headline: Amazon reportedly weighing a second multibillion-dollar investment in Anthropic
items.summary: Amazon is said to be considering another large investment in Anthropic while pushing the AI lab to lean more heavily on Amazon's in-house Trainium chips rather than Nvidia GPUs, deepening the cloud giant's strategic stake in Claude as it competes for AI infrastructure share.

items.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft jointly invest $15B in Anthropic as it becomes first AI lab on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud
items.summary: Anthropic signed a roughly $30B deal to deploy Claude on AWS while Nvidia and Microsoft jointly put $15B into the company, making it the first major AI lab to offer its models across all three big cloud platforms and pushing its valuation toward $350B.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly weighing another $1B investment in Figure AI's humanoid robots
items.summary: Nvidia is said to be considering a further roughly $1 billion investment in humanoid-robot maker Figure as the company expands its AI infrastructure and production capacity, building on an earlier compute partnership that could bring it up to 100,000 Nvidia GPUs.

items.headline: GXO and Agility Robotics to expand humanoid robot deployments to two more US warehouses
items.summary: Logistics firm GXO and robotics maker Agility Robotics announced plans to add humanoid robots to two additional US facilities starting in early 2027, extending an existing warehouse deployment as companies push to prove commercial viability for humanoid labor.

items.headline: Figure AI signs $3.5B Nscale compute deal for up to 100,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs
items.summary: Humanoid-robotics company Figure struck a multi-year partnership with cloud provider Nscale, committing $3.5B (scalable to over $6B) for up to 100,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs, with Nscale also taking an equity stake and becoming Figure's preferred compute provider for training its Helix robot-control models.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils "Dots," persistent always-on AI agents, at DevDay 2026
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Dots, named AI assistants that keep running inside ChatGPT after a user closes the app, each given its own cloud compute environment and the ability to carry context across multiple ongoing projects, alongside a new $500-per-month Pro tier with a premium speed option.
